About me

I am a telecommunications engineer, a graduate of the École Nationale Supérieure des Postes et Télécommunications (ENSPT), and I am now continuing my studies in France at 3iL Ingénieurs.

What drew me to cybersecurity is the role of the protector: understanding how an infrastructure is built in order to defend it against people who try to attack it. My projects reflect this: directory services, single sign-on, monitoring and server hardening.

In the longer term, I am moving towards AI security. AI is becoming the core of IT systems, and it can be corrupted or misused, for example through training data poisoning. I want to help companies protect the integrity of the AI systems they build and defend themselves against attackers who use AI.

Security and identity7-milestone project

Single sign-on with Keycloak

A central identity provider for all of the company's applications, backed by Active Directory.

  • Single sign-on for domain users
  • Directory federated over LDAPS, certificate verified
  • Second factor (TOTP, WebAuthn) enforced by role
  • Sensitive accounts and passwords cleaned up

Project screenshots

KeycloakSSOLDAPSActive DirectoryMFAPKIKeePassXC
See the steps
  1. DNS record for the identity provider, checked from the domain controller.
  2. Audit of the existing setup: AD accounts, administrators, inactive accounts, service accounts, Linux accounts and MariaDB databases.
  3. Fixes: KeePassXC vault, dedicated service account, dated quarantine of an inactive account, password rotation.
  4. Keycloak 26 installation, dedicated realm, removal of the temporary admin account.
  5. Directory federation over LDAPS and sign-in tests.
  6. Internal certificate authority: service certificates, distributed to workstations through GPO.
  7. Nextcloud and the time clock app connected, validated end to end.
  8. Role-based strong authentication (TOTP, WebAuthn, recovery codes), brute-force detection and sign-in event logging.
  9. Report: architecture, access matrix, authentication policy, residual risks.
Systems and directorySecure infrastructure

Active Directory and LDAP integration

Building the company directory and connecting web applications to domain authentication.

  • Directory structured into organisational units
  • Nextcloud and the time clock connected to AD
  • Authentication failure diagnosed and fixed

Project screenshots

Windows ServerAD DSGPOPowerShellNextcloud
See the steps
  1. Organisational units, users and business groups created; SamAccountName, UPN and email attributes corrected.
  2. Group Policy (GPO): 12-character minimum passwords, account lockout after 5 failed attempts.
  3. Sign-in auditing in the domain controller's Event Viewer.
  4. Nextcloud connected to AD through an LDAP service account.
  5. Troubleshooting a user who could not be found: root cause isolated by testing (missing displayName attribute), fix applied.
  6. PHP time clock app connected to the directory, and a “directory unavailable” error fixed.

HTTPS reverse proxy

All internal applications published behind a single server, without disrupting the sites already in service.

  • One site per hostname, all over HTTPS
  • Domain DNS records in place
  • Secure remote administration access

Project screenshots

Apache mod_proxyTLSDNSSSH
